newsitem.title: USA: Georgians approve several tax referendums.
newsitem.headline: Georgians approve several tax referendums.

text.p: In addition to the amendment allowing school districts to seek sales tax hikes for construction, Georgia voters approved several other statewide referendums that affect taxes, elections officials said Friday.

Voters approved constitutional Amendment 1, which repealed the state's intangible property tax on stocks and bonds. The vote was largely moot because the legislature had already repealed the after a court challenge, but the amendment will prevent them from ever reviving it.
Amendment 3 passed, allowing local governments to grant tax breaks to businesses that create jobs in economically depressed communities.
Voters also approved Amendment 5, which allows Chatham County to increase taxes on Hutchinson Island in Savannah to help pay for growth.
Additionally, Georgia voters apprpoved a pair of referendums exempting church-owned and school-owned buses, and property owned by Masonic lodges from taxation.
But voters rejected Amendment 4, which would have allowed cotton gin operators to tax themselves to raise money to train workers and promote their industry.
